patch:
--- a/SKILL.md
+++ b/SKILL.md
@@ -26 +26 @@
-1. Identify and search for the exact requested target. If it is not visible, run a single-pass sweep that spreads across distinct receptacle families rather than exhausting or looping over one type. Open each closed container (cabinet, drawer, fridge, etc.) once upon reaching it and read its contents; if it lacks the target, continue to a receptacle you have not yet inspected. Use your most recent observations to avoid returning to a receptacle you just confirmed empty. When one family (for example drawers) yields nothing, switch to a different uninspected family (such as cabinets, shelves, countertops/other surfaces, or appliances) before revisiting any earlier location. Keep the sweep within the step budget so that unopened containers and uninspected surfaces are checked before any loop back. Do not repeatedly check inventory while carrying nothing. Continue until the exact target is found or all plausible candidate receptacles have been inspected once.
+1. Identify and search for the exact requested target. If it is not visible, run a single forward sweep that uses the current observation, the admissible commands, your recent observations, and numbered receptacle names to choose the next move; do not rely on a global visited set. Treat each inspected receptacle as consumed for your immediate next move: the next move should go to a different receptacle, ideally one not just inspected. Use numbered receptacle names as a local progress cue: after checking an instance of a family, prefer the next higher-numbered instance, or a different family or open surface, instead of jumping back to a location seen in your last two observations. Early in the sweep, before committing to a long sequence in one family, prefer a currently listed open surface (countertop, desk, bed, diningtable, shelf, or similar) that has not just been observed as empty. After two consecutive inspected instances of the same family yield no target, switch to a different family or open surface rather than checking a third same-family instance. Open each closed container (cabinet, drawer, fridge, etc.) once upon reaching it and read its contents; if it lacks the target, continue forward to a new receptacle rather than cycling back through earlier ones. Keep the sweep within the step budget so that unopened containers and uninspected surfaces are checked before any loop back. Do not repeatedly check inventory while carrying nothing. Continue until the exact requested category is found or all plausible candidate receptacles have been inspected once.
@@ -28,2 +28,3 @@
-3. Acquire the exact target. If the task requires the object to be clean, carry it to an appropriate cleaning receptacle such as a sinkbasin and perform the clean action. If no cleaning is requested, skip the cleaning detour.
-4. Go directly to the requested destination. Open it first if it is closed, then place or move the target there. Do not detour to unrelated receptacles or release the target before the requested placement is completed.
+3. Acquire the exact target. If the task requires the object to be clean, carry it to an appropriate cleaning receptacle such as a sinkbasin and perform the clean action. If the task requires the object to be cooled or heated, carry the held exact target to the required appliance (fridge to cool, microwave to heat) and condition it: check the current admissible commands first, and if the explicit cool-X-with-fridge or heat-X-with-microwave action is listed while you hold the exact target, perform it immediately, even if the appliance is closed, without inserting the target. If it is not listed, open the appliance once and check again; if it is listed while you hold the target at the open appliance, perform it now without placing the target inside. Only if it is still not listed while holding at the open appliance, place the target inside once, then take it back once and perform the action while holding; never replace the conditioning action with closing and reopening the appliance or with repeated remove/reinsert cycles. Perform exactly one conditioning action, then carry the target to the requested destination (opening it if closed) and place it there; if the conditioning appliance is also the destination, condition the target and then place it there. If neither cleaning nor cooling/heating is requested, skip these detours.
+4. Go directly to the requested destination. Open it first if it is closed, then place or move the target there. Do not detour to unrelated receptacles or release the target before the requested placement is completed.
+5. For ordinary multi-instance placement: when the task requires two or more instances of the exact category, deliver them sequentially. After placing the first exact instance at the destination, continue searching (from remaining uninspected receptacles or a known source) for another instance of the same exact category and repeat until the requested count is placed. Do not stop after one, do not substitute a differently named near-match, and do not apply the desklamp rule of finishing with one co-located target to ordinary multi-instance put tasks.
reason: Revised the search step to require a forward sweep guided by current and recent observations and numbered receptacle names without a global visited set; added the cool/heat conditioning rule to step 3; and added a sequential multi-instance delivery step, while preserving exact-category matching, desklamp-scoped rules, and general acquisition/placement behavior.
